title: Priming staircase and seed-management: a deterministic throughput-spec
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note defines a practical, deterministic throughput benchmarking spec focused on two frequently entangled sources of non-repeatability: priming (cache/KV warmup) and randomization seed management for the load generator. Target audience: serving-runtime engineers running model throughput experiments, performance reviewers, and SRE partners validating capacity claims. The aim is repeatable, debuggable runs that surface throughput cliff-points and non-linear scaling under steady-state and transition loads.

Motivation (short):
- We frequently see run-to-run throughput variance that masks regressions.
- Cold-start priming and inconsistent RNG seeds in loadgens are the most common causes.
- A repeatable harness must make priming deterministic or explicitly quantify residual nondeterminism.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Priming: any pre-run actions that fill caches (KV cache, tokenizer caches, GPU memory allocation patterns) or otherwise change the first N tokens cost profile.
- Deterministic seed: a fixed RNG seed for all sources of randomness in the load generator and the priming trace sampler.
- Ramp staircase: stepwise concurrency increases with overlapping measurement windows to decouple priming effects from steady throughput.
- Seed sweep: running a small, fixed set of different seeds to estimate residual stochastic variance.

Overview of the recommended experiment flow:
1) Environment checklist (must pass):
   - Node images and runtime release pinned (image SHA).
   - Model artifact and model-version id pinned.
   - Kernel selection/logging enabled (if applicable).
   - System-level telemetry (nvidia-smi, io stats, kernel dmesg) collection enabled.
   - Time sync verified (NTP) and clock skew < 100ms across hosts.

2) Deterministic priming plan:
   - Use a replay log derived from production prefixes (anonymized) whenever possible. This replay log is the canonical priming artifact for the model+version.
   - If production logs are not available, synthesize a deterministic prefix set: N=200 unique prefixes covering short/long/edge cases; store them as priming.json and commit to the experiment bundle.
   - Apply the same ordering and seeds to the priming replay. Do not shuffle unless the seed explicitly encodes the shuffle order.
   - Priming intensity: aim to execute enough requests such that cumulative token generation exceeds the typical KV cache capacity threshold for the model (empirically ~5x typical cache keys). Example: for Llama-like model 7B, run priming traffic that produces ~200k cached tokens. Document the token count.

3) Staircase ramp and measurement windows: rationale and config
   - Staircase profile: concurrency steps [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96] or tailored to instance GPU count. Each step is composed of: 60s warm window (to allow transient buffers), 180s measurement window, 30s cool-down where traffic is reduced to 0.
   - Overlap warm windows: start the next higher concurrency warm period 30s before the prior measurement window ends to detect hysteresis. This overlap helps us catch cases where cache eviction or backend spilling occurs across steps.
   - Measurement aggregation: discard first 30s of the measurement window for p50/p95/p99 computation (to remove short transients).
   - Steady-state requirement: for a step to be considered stable, the moving average of throughput over the last 60s must vary < 3% and p95 latency must not drift by more than 5% during the 180s window.

4) RNG seed policy and repeatability enforcement
   - Single-run determinism: pick a canonical seed (e.g., 42-snowball) for the primary experiment. Log RNG seed value in experiment metadata and in loadgen stdout. The loadgen must derive all randomness (query selection, token-level jitter, inter-arrival Poisson sampling) from this single seed.
   - Seed sweep: repeat the full staircase with 3 additional seeds [42, 1234, 2025, 77777] to estimate residual nondeterminism. If variance exceeds the acceptance criteria (see metrics), investigate.
   - Seed replayability: retain the seed and the PRNG algorithm name in the artifacts so a run can be reproduced months later.

5) Priming variants and controlled experiments
   - Cold priming: no priming run. Use only if you want to measure worst-case first-request cost.
   - Deterministic priming: canonical replay log as above. Use this for all regression comparisons.
   - Hot priming (production-like): continuous stream of priming traffic for 30 minutes prior to staircase to emulate long-running production conditions. Useful for long-lived caches and GPU memory fragmentation effects.
   - Hybrid priming: deterministic replay + random small jitter (seeded) applied to timestamps to model arrival variability while keeping content deterministic.

6) Metrics and acceptance criteria
   - Primary throughput metric: sustained tokens-per-second measured over measurement window (180s), reported as mean + 95% CI across runs.
   - Stability target: for a baseline run (canonical seed + deterministic priming) we expect three independent runs to have mean throughput within ±3% and throughput standard deviation < 2% of mean.
   - Latency guardrails: p95 latency must not increase by >10% at any concurrency step compared to baseline.
   - Regression flagging: if mean throughput drops >4% or std dev increases >2x vs baseline, fail the regression.

7) Statistical analysis and tests (practical)
   - Report mean, median, stddev, min, max, and 90/95/99 percentiles for throughput and latency per step.
   - Use Levene's test (or Bartlett where appropriate) to detect changes in variance between baseline and candidate.
   - For non-normal distributions prefer non-parametric tests (Mann-Whitney U) when comparing central tendency.
   - Provide confidence intervals using bootstrap resampling of per-request token counts across the measurement window.

8) Diagnostics to collect and correlate
   - Loadgen: per-request trace id, seed value, selected prefix id, timestamp, inter-arrival sample, batch size, measured RTT to fronting load-balancer.
   - Serving: per-shard queue depths, batch composition histograms, kernel selection logs, memory allocation histograms, KV cache hit rates (per-key), metered token accounting.
   - Infra: GPU utilization (smoothed 1s), SM occupancy, memory allocator fragmentation, NIC drops, syscall latencies.
   - Correlation approach: align traces by timestamp and compute per-request latency vs backend batch size and cache hit. Surface anomalies where single-request latency spikes align with evictions or large batch formation.

9) Failure modes and how to triage quickly
   - Large run-to-run variance but identical seeds: check environment drift (kernel version, driver), noisy co-tenants, or nondeterministic kernel selection.
   - Stepwise degradation at moderate concurrency: inspect batching histograms for pathological batch sizes (e.g., many oversized batches causing memory pressure).
   - Throughput cliffs at higher concurrency: check for GC or allocator stalls, spilling to host memory, or hypervisor scheduler interference.

10) Example canonical loadgen config (YAML-like, deterministic)
   ---
   loadgen_version: v2
   seed: 42
   priming: "replay/priming.json"  # canonical priming artifact
   priming_mode: deterministic
   priming_token_target: 200000
   staircase_steps: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64]
   step_warm_sec: 60
   step_measure_sec: 180
   step_cool_sec: 30
   overlap_warm_sec: 30
   arrival_process: poisson  # seeded RNG
   batch_bias: fixed  # use deterministic batch selection where possible
   log_level: info
   collect_traces: true
   trace_sample_rate: 0.05
   output_dir: experiments/2025-02-20/seed-42
   ---

11) Artifact hygiene
   - Store the following in the experiment bundle: machine image SHA, model artifact id, loadgen binary SHA, priming.json, seed value, staircase config file, raw telemetry compressed, and a short narrative describing anything special about the run (spot instance usage, infra changes).

12) Post-run checklist and reporting
   - Confirm all three canonical runs completed without infra errors.
   - Run the seed sweep runs and compute variability.
   - Attach summarized CSV with per-step metrics and the raw telemetry tar.gz to the experiment ticket.
   - If variance is high, schedule an infra-isolated run on dedicated hardware and repeat.

13) Quick reference acceptance thresholds (copyable):
   - Repeatability: mean throughput change across identical-seed runs < 3% over 3 runs.
   - Stability: stddev < 2% of mean throughput.
   - Latency regression: p95 increase < 10% per step.
   - Noise tolerance for seed sweep: median throughput shift < 2% across seeds.

Appendix A — lightweight troubleshooting commands (examples):
- collect nvidia smi loop: while true; do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv -l 1 >> gpu-telemetry.csv; done
- check kernel messages: dmesg --ctime | tail -n 100
- batch histogram from serving logs: awk -F"," '{print $5}' batches.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head

Appendix B — short experiment templates (copy/paste)
- Quick smoke (fast): staircase_steps: [1,4,16,64], step_measure_sec: 60, seed: 2025
- Long stability (overnight): staircase_steps scaled to peak, step_measure_sec: 900, priming_mode: hot, repeat: 5 runs

Checklist before merging results to main benchmark page:
- [ ] Experiment bundle uploaded to s3/bench-artifacts and link added to ticket
- [ ] All telemetry files compressed and checksum recorded
- [ ] Seed and priming.json checked into experiment manifest
- [ ] Statistical report attached (CSV + pdf summary)

Notes and open questions:
- We should standardize a canonical priming set per model family (open task).
- Investigate whether kernel-selection nondeterminism is a frequent root cause and whether we can make kernel selection deterministic or more heavily instrumented.
- Consider adding an automated post-run detector that triggers infra-isolated reruns when variance exceeds thresholds.

Author notes: this spec attempts to be minimally prescriptive but maximally repeatable. The deterministic priming + seed policy plus the staircase with overlapping warms is an operational pattern that has caught several subtle regressions in the past. Please review for missing telemetry hooks or acceptance thresholds that do not fit certain models.
